input: Track every purchase in cash for two weeks

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether to track only physical cash or also digital equivalents (e.g., cash apps, prepaid cards) defines the boundaries of what gets logged.
Whether this is for personal spending only or includes a household/family changes how entries are categorised and attributed.
Knowing when the two-week window starts determines the immediate first action and any prep needed before day one.
A spending limit or budget target the user is trying to stay within would shape how the data is presented and what alerts are useful.
The level of detail captured per purchase (amount only vs. category, location, notes) affects the tracking method and effort required.
The tool or format used — paper notebook, spreadsheet, phone app — determines the entire workflow and friction level of daily logging.
Understanding what the user wants to do with the data at the end (cut spending, spot patterns, build a budget) shapes what summary or output to produce.

gold.taskTitle: Track every cash purchase for two weeks
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to log all cash-based transactions they make over a two-week period, likely to gain visibility into their spending habits.

questions.title: Does "cash" mean physical notes only, or digital cash too?
questions.description: Clarify whether the scope includes only physical banknotes and coins, or also cash-equivalent methods like prepaid cards, Venmo, or cash-back payments.

questions.title: Is this tracking your spending alone or a whole household?
questions.description: Determine whether only the user's personal purchases are logged, or if a partner, family members, or housemates are included.

questions.title: Which specific two-week period are you starting this?
questions.description: Pin down the exact start date so the plan, reminders, and end-of-period review can be scheduled accurately.

questions.title: Is there a weekly or total spending limit you are targeting?
questions.description: Establish whether the user has a budget ceiling in mind, which would influence how spending is flagged or summarised during the period.

questions.title: What details do you want to log per purchase?
questions.description: Decide the granularity of each entry — amount only, or also category, merchant name, time of day, and optional notes.

questions.title: Where do you want to record each purchase as it happens?
questions.description: Identify the preferred logging tool — a phone app, spreadsheet, notes app, paper journal — to design the right daily workflow.

questions.title: What do you plan to do with the data at the end?
questions.description: Understand the end goal — spotting spending patterns, building a monthly budget, cutting a specific habit — so the two-week summary is useful and actionable.
